channel.title: Horizons: medication safety in digital systems
channel.description: Medication safety alerts involving digital systems, collated from regulators, safety organisations and standards bodies worldwide.

item.title: HSSIB: Procurement, usability and adoption of ‘smart’ infusion pumps
item.description: Although the aim of smart infusion pumps is to improve patient safety, the technology can introduce new risks. This investigation focused on understanding the challenges involved in introducing smart infusion pump technology within NHS hospitals.

item.title: HSSIB: Electronic prescribing and medicines administration systems and safe discharge
item.description: We’ve identified a significant safety risk posed by poorly implemented electronic prescribing and medicines administration (ePMA) systems. An ePMA system supports the safe, effective, and cost-effective use of medicines from a patient’s admission to hospital until their discharge.

item.title: Läkemedelsverket: Gemensam övning ska stärka beredskapen vid läkemedelsbrist
item.description: Hur kan myndigheter och företag tillsammans upprätthålla läkemedelsförsörjningen när det till exempel sker cyberangrepp, sjukvården är hårt belastad och krig bryter ut i Sveriges närområde? Det var delar av scenariot när ett trettiotal deltagare samlades i Uppsala den 21–‍22 oktober för att öva krisledning, samverkan och kommunikation. Övningen omfattade läkemedel för både människor och djur.

item.title: Drug Safety Update: #MedSafetyWeek (2 to 8 November 2026): Don't ignore suspected side effects, report them! Updates to the Yellow Card website and app
item.description: The annual #MedSafetyWeek campaign is taking place from 2 to 8 November 2026 to promote the importance of reporting side effects from medicines and medical device incidents. This year's theme is ‘Side effects: don't ignore them, report them!’

item.title: HSSIB: Online prescribing: challenges and opportunities to improve patient safety
item.description: This investigation looks at the complex regulatory landscape around independent online prescribing and challenges sharing patient information between the NHS and independent online prescribing services.

Root cause: Software design (manufacturing process).

item.title: FDA Software recalls: Device recall: LifeShield Drug Library Management (DLM), LifeShield Infusion Safety Software Suite v2.2 Product No. 17003-02
item.description: ICU Medical, Inc.. Software issue only allows Concentration Limits to be defined to one digit of precision past the decimal point (0.1) instead of three digits (0.001). If the user is unable to use Concentration Limits as intended, they may need to change the limits to something other than what is recommended by the drug manufacturer, which may result in over- or under-delivery. Root cause: Software Design Change.

item.title: FDA Software recalls: Device recall: LifeShield Drug Library Management (DLM); LifeShield Infusion Safety Software Suite v2.2 List Number 17003-02
item.description: ICU Medical, Inc.. For certain customers, the Change Summary review option ceases to operate as expected for any migrated library after the migration has been completed. Users must use alternate methods to review changes. Failure to do so may lead in over delivery, under delivery, or delay in setup on the infusion pump. Root cause: Software Design Change.

item.title: HSSIB: Electronic patient record (EPR) systems – thematic review
item.description: We have completed a thematic review of 50 HSSIB reports to identify specific patient safety issues and learning related to electronic patient record (EPR) systems. The report includes a safety observation and local-level learning prompts around safe selection and procurement, implementation and ongoing optimisation of EPR systems.
